title: Higher peripheral blood homocysteine levels are associated with schizophrenia: evidence from a case-control study and a meta-analysis
title_zh: 血液中同型半胱氨酸水平升高与精神分裂症相关：来自病例对照研究和荟萃分析的证据
abstract: Several studies suggest that homocysteine is associated with schizophrenia (SCZ), but existing evidence has been limited by small sample sizes. We aimed to investigate the association between blood homocysteine levels and schizophrenia. We conducted a case-control study followed by a meta-analysis. In the case-control study, 1159 patients with SCZ diagnosed according to DSM-5 (mean age 22.6 ± 8.4 years; 51.9% male) and 1440 healthy controls (HC) (mean age 38.4 ± 9.7 years; 51.3% male) were recruited. Plasma homocysteine levels were measured using an AU5800 automated biochemical analyzer and compared between groups. For the meta-analysis, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were systematically searched through February 2024 for case-control studies comparing blood homocysteine levels between patients with SCZ and HC. Ratios of means (RoM) with 95% confidence intervals were pooled using random effects models. In the case-control study, patients with SCZ had significantly higher homocysteine levels than HC (14.4 [11.3-21.6] vs. 12.3 [10.1-15.7] µmol/L; P < 0.001), and the association remained significant after adjustment for age and sex. Consistently, the meta-analysis of 54 case-control studies including 9781 participants (4526 patients with SCZ and 5255 HC) showed significantly higher homocysteine levels in patients with SCZ than in HC (RoM 1.34, 95% CI 1.28-1.41; P < 0.001). Subgroup analyses stratified by disease course, sample type, sex, study region, and homocysteine measurement method yielded consistent results. Blood homocysteine levels are elevated in patients with SCZ in both the case-control analysis and meta-analysis. These preliminary findings suggest a possible association between homocysteine and SCZ, although further well-controlled prospective and longitudinal studies are needed to clarify its clinical significance.
abstract_zh: 多项研究提示同型半胱氨酸与精神分裂症（SCZ）之间存在关联，但现有证据因样本量小而受到限制。本研究旨在调查血液同型半胱氨酸水平与精神分裂症的关联。我们进行了病例对照研究后进行荟萃分析。在病例对照研究中，招募了1159例根据DSM-5诊断的SCZ患者（平均年龄22.6±8.4岁；男性51.9%）和1440例健康对照组（HC，平均年龄38.4±9.7岁；男性51.3%）。使用AU5800自动生化分析仪测量血浆同型半胱氨酸水平并比较组间差异。在荟萃分析中，我们通过系统检索PubMed、Embase、Cochrane Library和Web of Science，截至2024年2月，寻找比较SCZ患者与HC血液同型半胱氨酸水平的病例对照研究。使用随机效应模型汇总均值比（RoM）及其95%置信区间。在病例对照研究中，SCZ患者的同型半胱氨酸水平显著高于HC（14.4 [11.3-21.6] vs. 12.3 [10.1-15.7] µmol/L；P < 0.001），且在调整年龄和性别后结果仍显著一致。荟萃分析共纳入54项病例对照研究，共9781名参与者（4526例SCZ患者和5255例HC），结果显示SCZ患者的同型半胱氨酸水平显著高于HC（RoM 1.34，95% CI 1.28-1.41；P < 0.001）。按疾病进程、样本类型、性别、研究区域和同型半胱氨酸测定方法进行的亚组分析均得到一致结果。病例对照分析和荟萃分析均显示SCZ患者血液中同型半胱氨酸水平升高。这些初步发现提示同型半胱氨酸与SCZ之间可能存在关联，尽管需要进一步的良好控制的前瞻性和纵向研究来阐明其临床意义。
